title: Using Case-Based Reasoning to Predict Marathon Performance and Recommend Tailored Training Plans
authors: Feely C, Caulfield B, Lawlor A, Smyth B
journal: Case-Based Reasoning Research and Development (ICCBR 2020), Lecture Notes in Computer Science
population: Marathon runners' training/workout and race histories (>21,000 runners, 1.5 million sessions)
findings: A case-based reasoning system uses a case base of training/workouts and race histories to predict future marathon times for a target runner throughout training, to calibrate progress and plan race-day pacing.
It recommends tailored training plans adapted to the runner's current goal-time target, based on the plans of similar runners who achieved that time.
Evaluated on a dataset of more than 21,000 unique runners and 1.5 million training sessions; the abstract states no accuracy numbers.
limitations: Observational app data; no randomized or injury outcomes; imitation of similar runners is not causal proof; no quantitative results in the abstract; conference chapter not in PubMed.
implications: Similar-runner retrieval (recent volume, fitness, goal time) can seed typical weekly volumes and long-run progressions but must sit under explicit safety caps.
Re-predict goal time as new training data arrive and adjust the plan.
Use cohort distributions as priors, not targets to exceed.
